author: high
claim: Direct subgoal solved: a bipartite graph has no odd cycle.
evidence: Let the two bipartition classes be fixed. Along a cycle, every traversed edge changes the class containing the current vertex. Hence after an odd number of edges the current vertex lies in the class opposite the starting vertex, whereas the final vertex of the cycle equals the starting vertex. Therefore the cycle length is even. author: high
claim: Direct subgoal solved: a graph with no odd cycle is bipartite.
evidence: In each connected component choose a root and divide vertices by parity of shortest-path distance from the root. If an edge joined two vertices in the same parity class, shortest root paths to its endpoints together with the edge and reversal of the second root path would be an odd closed walk. Verified fact ec5be0d896864f8c implies that such a walk contains an odd cycle, contradicting the hypothesis. Therefore every edge crosses the two parity classes.
